speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you've been having trouble sleeping where you wake up frightened. To help me understand what's happening, can you tell me if you feel like you're running or flying during these episodes, and do you notice any sweating or a racing heart?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the preservation of alertness and ability to be consoled quickly suggests these aren't nightmares. Can you describe exactly what happens in these episodes, do you or anyone else snore loudly, and do you have any history of bedwetting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.
